Using the designations and mentioning the recovery before actually saying what the objects are (in the 3rd paragraph no less) is a huge pet peeve of mine. This alone would warrant a downvote on any skip, no matter how brilliantly well-written it would otherwise be. Then there's the interview transcript, which I saw others enjoyed: it brings nothing new to the table (we already know the effects from the researcher-doctor text convo) and it makes sense that as soon as someone noticed the issue it be removed and rewritten properly.

I don't expect anyone to fix these issues since it's been so long since the article was written (which would normally rend this a necropost, for which I apologise), but if it happens I'll change my vote. Till then, however, it's a very firm downvote

item.title: The Lost Holiday Special
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: (Joke) SCP

Genre (Optional): Comedy, Weird

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP, extensive addenda describing discoveries.

Elevator Pitch: Finally, an answer to where all those Lost Christmas specials come from, where the end up, and why they're all so awful. This extensive research demonstrates both the anomalous nature of their appearance, and offers an occult explanation for their poor quality and untimely release.

Central Narrative: Although the '78 Star Wars special is probably the best known, some paranormal entity has been producing anomalous media since at least 1976. The addenda include selected summaries such as "The 007 Days of Christmas" (1976), "A Very Rocky Christmas" (1979), "The Blues Brothers: A Mission From God" (1998), and "The Festivus Reunion" (2015), all featuring appropriately aged (or decayed) actors reprising their original roles.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Let's be honest. The universe would be a better place if we could blame every holiday special on some unknowable force.

Additional Notes: G. D! B B, A GG C B B A A G.

item.title: The Sandman (GREENLIGHT WANTED)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Elevator Pitch: An 8ft humanoid that was discovered in Denmark with talons, sharp claws, a split jaw, █ █████ that appear to be some sort organic ████ as well as a very thin 4-meter wide cloud of anomalous dust that surrounds the humanoid. This cloud of dust appears to make subjects incredibly drowsy and can be blown towards the nearest subject using the █ █████ on itself and within a 5-second threshold, the affected subjects will fall asleep. Both the humanoid and dust cloud can only be seen when UV rays are shined at them. When asleep the subject will find themselves someplace with sand where the entity will be able to shapeshift using the sand around it into someone that the subject is fond of. Once the entity is spotted by the subject they will be drawn to the entity. When the subject approaches the entity, it will shapeshift into an embodiment of the subject’s worst fears while still embodying one or few of its original traits usually only the split jaw. The entity will then ████████ and ██████ the subject which afterward the subject will wake up. 3 to 8 hours after the subject wakes up all the injuries the subject sustained will happen instantaneously, killing the subject.

Central Narrative: On 9/14/15 from 2 am to 9 am 27 reports were made of people being instantaneously mutilated with what appears to be 3 3-inch ████ █████ on their head. All bodies have been found to have been within a 20-mile radius of Amager Strandpark. On 9/19/15 at 3:55 pm, an 8ft humanoid was discovered to be walking around Amager Strandpark. The entity was later contained that day by █████████.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Entity based on the Ole Lukøje that connects a subject’s experience in their dream world to reality. "It dragged me into my nightmare where it wished for all to feed its slumbering strength."

Additional Notes: I’d like feedback especially on how to better word the central narrative and how to make a better hook. When the date the entity was contained is put into the DD/MM/YYYY (a format that some countries in Europe use) would be 19/9/15 (19-9-15) which is a letter cipher for SiO2. SiO2 is the chemical formula for the compound silicon dioxide (the most common component in sand). The other date also has significance. The name will be Mr. Sandman or The Sandman.

item.title: Admin Post - Info - Open
item.content:encoded:
Obligatory note to please keep any responses to the post above civil.

To other authors who are struggling with receiving feedback, please make use of the resources available, including the IRC chatrooms for real-time feedback, staff members who can match you with reviewers if you're having difficulty finding readers, and other authors with whom you can trade drafts for critique.

Additionally, rather than writing vehement posts like this which will disappear if the page is slated for standard deletion, you can state complaints here: http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/forum/t-5797485/complaints-thread or contact a staff member about the situation.

Also, as an aside, one's forum posts can be read via the "recent posts and comments" section of a wikidot profile. Misrepresentation of reviewer interactions doesn't really encourage reviewers to want to assist an author.


Forum category: Per Page Discussions / Per page discussions
Forum thread: SCP-5136

Hoo boy…

Here's a crit.
On a pale horse...

SCP-5129 is to be kept in a 15m x 15m Titanium room

Aaand that's a downvote. Titanium shouldn't be capitalized. Horses generally need two acres of land- about 8km2 of land. 15mx15m is about 225m, far too small. Finally, titanium is only useful if you need something both light and strong. Otherwise, reinforced steel is almost always going to be better.

Steel shackles are to be locked to SCP-5129 hind legs to at least slow it down.

… how? I mean, how is this supposed to slow it down? Also; bad tone. "The rear legs of SCP-5129 are to be shackled to inhibit its maximum speed" is better.

Reinforced sliding steel doors are locked in place when SCP-5129 goes on its rampage.

… See, now this would be an appropriate use of titanium or (more likely) a steel/titanium alloy. Regardless, unless material requirements are of the "substitutes WILL cause a breach" nature, you're likeoy better off not mentioning them.

Also, "rampaging" or rage states aren't really seen as interesting. They're boting, and generally never used now.

Two foundation agents who have taken courses on exorcism and have been dispatched by their teacher are to be kept at SCP-5129's containment cell at all times.

… what kind of exorcism? Shinto exorcisms are much different than catholic exorcisms. Furthermore, based on the SCP, it's unclear how an exorcist or someone with exorcist training would help here, as the idea of an exorcist is to banish evil spirits/demons from a host, object, or place.

As for the SCP itself, you've basically failed to understand ancient greek mythology. They have three seperate sections of Hades, the underworld. First, the greeks had Elisyum, a paradise where the truly blessed and honored would go upon death. Then you have Tartarus, their equivalent of hell where the Titans and those who commited truly reprehensible acts would go for eternal torment. Finally, you had Asphereus, where everyone else went; neither reward nor punishment, the souls of people sent here would be wandering aimlessly, forever caught up in the moment of their demise unless stirred out of it by mortals visiting the place.

None of these places are said to resemble what you described in the exploration.

Furthermore, a creature like this would most likely be associated with Ares, the God of War, not Hades, the God of Death, considering its habit to raid and pillage its local environs.

I strongly recommend you go to the site forums and work on the core concept of this, rather than go to the draft stage. The flaws of this SCP are fundamental in nature, beyond what I've mentioned, and attempting to draft it without focusing on the core concepts first will make it harder to fix.

item.title: Re: Looking for Greenlight: The God Pen
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there undeadmuffin. Let’s take a look at your concept.

+ crit
- crit

So on the surface this seems like an overly-simple concept: you have a basic compulsion effect (the pen forces the writer to think/write whatever it’s thinking). You also have a simple page outline where you’ve listed some examples of what the pen will be writing (I’m assuming these will come across on the page as journal entries detailing the pen’s prior life).

I’m left wondering if that’s all to the concept… Because if so, it’s not a very compelling article on its own. You yourself have mentioned that it’s “ink pen meets Forrest Gump,”, so what’s so different about the story compared to that of the film? If you’re comparing it to a film, is there going to be a beginning, middle and end? Even, an article solely comprised of the pen’s backstory isn’t very compelling.

Basically, I’m pushing you to give us more. The concept on its own is workable, but the events you’ve described surrounding the anomaly isn’t very exciting at the moment.

Basically the fleeting and uncertainty of life as told by an ink pen that has gathered a number of life experiences over the decades.

This is an example of an idea / theme, but your article should not revolve around it by itself. Rather, it should come out through the story that you tell. Some more questions you can consider:

1. Who made the pen? Why did it trap itself within a pen in the first place? What goals did the entity have before it was trapped? What does it want now besides being mopey?

2. How does the Foundation contain it? There should be some difficulty here or consequence of containment failure. Does its existential thoughts influence the researchers it comes into contact with, for example? If it’s Thaumiel, how then will the scp be used by the Foundation?

3. What are you trying to say by the end of the article. Right now, the message is simply: life sucks. Is that really all you want the readers to feel?

If you decide to revise the concept further / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll try my best to reply. Best of luck!


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: Looking for Greenlight: The God Pen

Some crit:

A highly intelligent monster with no narrative and no discernible motive you say?
This feels like it comes right out of Series I.

"Central Narrative: None"

This is where the problem lies, what's the point? You create a monster who mimes and devours people when it tricks them into coming near and what, stick it in a box who cares? Why does any of this matter, it being a mime is just fluff if not given a reason, is there a backstory? Does a researcher go to lengths uncovering a backstory and this is told through personnel logs? There's nothing here.

"vicus"

I think you mean viscous, he's not spilling out Roman settlements when he bleeds, unless he is, that would be very, very interesting.

I see you are looking to create a narrative around this, and I highly encourage you to do so but don't rely on critters to think one up for you. Good luck author.

item.title: They Just Keep Searching
item.content:encoded:
Hey! I posted this one before, but that was well over two weeks ago and it didn't get any responses. Figured I might as well try this forum again before looking into other critique options :) (I have made some very slight modifications since, anyway).

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Pretty standard SCP article layout, but I’m going to make heavy use of drop-down “click to reveal” sections to help break down the length.

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a 1 m3 metal safe that cannot be opened or damaged by any apparent means. It causes auditory hallucinations in those who stand within 10 m of it for more than 3 hours (cumulative) that tempt them to try to open it. Eventually these victims convert into anomalous humanoids with an innate knowledge of SCP-XXXX’s location and high resistance to anaesthetic and amnestics. Each of these beings will stick to 1 of 2 distinct behaviour patterns:

  • SCP-XXXX-1 – “Searchers”. Will search obsessively for an alleged key to SCP-XXXX when able. Can become frustrated and violent at times. Lucid and capable of conversation, highly manipulative.
  • SCP-XXXX-2 – Animalistic. Repeatedly attempts to open SCP-XXXX by force, overriding any other behavioural drives. Incapable of conversation.
+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: Features an extensive discovery report on the first emergence of the later-named SCP-XXXX-1, leading to discovery of XXXX and XXXX-2. Also features a report on a recurring incident with SCP-XXXX that the Foundation is still studying. References are made to a specific named researcher and her hypotheses/findings at several points to help give a connected narrative feel.
Tried to give the article a progressive narrative, in that SCP-XXXX seems relatively simple at first but every new thing we learn makes it seem more and more trouble.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: As previously mentioned, progressive nature of the article meant to gradually increase intrigue.

An incident report states that motion sensors within cell are often tripped and cameras deactivated, only for guards to find the cell completely undisturbed and equipment behaving normally again once they get there (incident does not repeat when SCP-XXXX is under constant guard), suggesting perhaps SCP-XXXX is starting to show awareness and more physically active behaviours, or possibly just messing with electrical equipment (still being studied at “time of report”).

Section at end reveals that an SCP-XXXX-1 instance claimed SCP-XXXX’s area of effect would begin expanding, causing the Foundation to regularly test its size, but SCP-XXXX-1 may have been lying and no changes have yet been detected.

Basically, I’m trying to give the sense with both of these parts that this SCP may or may not be a ticking time bomb of sorts.

Additional Notes: This is my first SCP idea so I’m sure it has plenty of issues all over, so please fire away! I'm still trying to think of a better name for it.

item.title: Tower of Babel (SEEKING GREENLIGHT)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Occurs over several iterations, with the threat increasing over time

+ View Block
- Hide

Elevator Pitch: - A memetic effect which can be transferred through print, speech, or digital media.

-The infection causes all infected individuals to begin speaking in an info-hazardous language. Every 2 days infected individuals will become paralysed for an increasing period of time. Within 7 months this paralysis will become permanent.

-Individuals affected by the anomaly will be conscious during the period of paralysis, being somehow disconnected from their body and walking around in an incorporeal form. Within this form, they will be unable to communicate with any other affected individuals or non-affected individuals. When in this form, a massive black obelisk, which called Iskententhine (translating to 'That which is the end)

-Affected individuals are unaware of the memetic basis of their infection unless told, and as such are likely to speak to everyone as if speaking in normal English.

Central Narrative: -Anomaly is first thought to be safe, as an anomaly affecting the population of a factory near a city that doesn't exist (this is important), but soon is reclassified as Euclid as several foundation researchers and D-Class are infected (The Euclid level object is a new iteration). The foundation researchers are amneticised [[footnote]] This is spelled wrong]] and contained, but it is believed that one infection gets out, as the infection reappears in the high school where a researchers son lives.

-Object is re-classified as Keter after the infection is thought to be neutralised by aggressive foundation action, and efforts to bury all affected individuals. The effect re-appears in several different locations following this, and soon large swaths of humanity are infected. Several prominent foundation members move into secure facilities to wait out the disaster. SCP-2000 is activated, the foundation recommends suicide for all individuals and efforts from several Groups of interests create a 1km layer of dirt and dust over the original earth, creating new geological formations. Shortly after, the O5 leave the containment chamber, recreate humanity, and continue.

The final iterations object class is Cernunnos, and it seems that the infection has arisen again, in Site 102, Canberra, Australia.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Will the foundation sacrifice human communication permanently to save humanity?

Notes: I had a wildly different idea under the same name previously. This article is completely different from that (the only thing in common is the hook), so I've put it in a new thread.

item.title: Re: SCP Idea looking for greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Summoned by PM:

Hi there Noah J Cooper. Let’s take a look at your concept.

So my initial comment to you (through PM) was that the concept hasn’t been fleshed out fully, and I still stand by that assessment. You should endeavour to use all 400 words of the limit, and it’s a red flag if you haven’t done that: it usually means the concept isn’t able to stand on its two feet.

True to nature, I’m seeing a few issues with the concept, which I will list down below:

(1) When I read your elevator pitch, I don’t really understand the mechanics of how the scp operates. Okay, so it explodes and takes over people. What does it mean to “get access to all of the previous hosts memories” and how does the sphere “regenerate”? More importantly, why does this happen? What is the sphere’s purpose in doing this? All these questions could have been explored further.

(2) Under your “Central Narrative” segment, instead of telling us what could be shown in the logs, tell us explicitly what the story is. How exactly does the Foundation discover the scp and contain it? Do they experiment with the scp? What happens when they do? How does your article end? Give us specifics please.

(3) I don’t understand either what you mean at the end when you say “so in a way, it relies on the foundation to survive.” Perhaps it’s because I don’t understand how the scp functions in the first place, so I couldn’t see how the sphere relies on the Foundation to survive. Doesn’t it regenerate on its own as well? So again, I’m left scratching my head.

If you decide to revise the concept further / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll try my best to reply. Best of luck!

SCP can only viewed at night at designated platforms 350m below sea level. Videoing or photographing SCP-XXXX must be avoided as well as viewing it for more than 1 minute continuously, or making direct eye contact.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX was first alerted to the SCP foundation through a field agent located inside of NOAA. NOAA identified a drastic change in salinity in an area roughly 1km2 somewhere in the Atlantic. Field Agents Smith, Jones, Roger, Greeves and Alex investigated the site of this anomalous activity using a SCP ship Horizon. Upon arrival the agents confirmed a change in salinity within the area as well as mutated and aggressive versions of the local fauna and flora. All agents sent to investigate this anomalous area during this initial Expedition, never returned. The last contact with the foundation in the transcript logs ended with the lead agent Smith saying:

"It's in the water, its in my head, its on the boat… send Deep Feeders"
After a considerable loss of life and 3 more expeditions were the foundation able to secure SCP.

item.title: The Painter (Old Concept)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre (Optional): Horror.

Elevator Pitch: The Painter is a faceless humanoid male with little to no facial features, the exception being it's eyes, it is able to decide the (horrible and gruesome) fate of any living human by painting it on a canvas (fate as in the way they die). No matter how hard it's victims will try they will always meet their fate, this manipulates the world around the victim so that they will meet their fate no matter the cost, it's only limitation is that it must know how the victim looks like in order to put them on a canvas. The foundation is unable to take the paintbrush and the canvas of the Painter because it's own fate is to keep painting until the end of mankind itself, so any attempt in doing so will result in an inevitable failure because there will always be a series of unstoppable events that will result in the painter getting it's necessary tools for it to continue painting.

Central Narrative: The Painter's story is that it is the judge of humanity, it is here to create and manipulate everyone's fate, it decides how and when everyone will experience their final moments and it will not stop until everyone's fate is set. The foundation also needs to severely restrict the painter's knowledge of any other SCPs, just imagine the damage if it were to paint a scientist in the jaws of 682, a huge containment breach would have to happen in order for the scientist to meet their fate.

The Painter was originally found in a cabin in the woods after a few campers reported "a weird man painting them dying in horrible ways". After a few years all of the campers died exactly how they reported the paintings to look like and that's when the foundation stepped in, they used smoke grenades, thermal vision and a bag to blind the target and capture it, but being captured by the foundation was only part of it's fate, it will use the foundation's infinite resources in order to keep painting.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The article will contain a few of the many victims of the Painter and how they met their grim fate, how the foundation will conduct tests on the painter and how it's anomalous world manipulation effect had a change on the world and the foundation.

Additional Notes: This is an old idea, my first one actually, I made an old thread about it almost a year ago and I'm trying to revisit the concept and improve it. hopefully I will be able to achieve that, if you decide to visit the old thread and find that you like the original concept more or some ideas from it, just let me know.

item.title: The Infinite Beach (Seeking Greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Anomalous section of California coastline which demonstrates non-euclidean terrain, as you can walk all you want and never get any closer to the water, which appears to be only 90-ish yards away. It gets a little more interesting, trust me.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up a lot of space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): N/A

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP Article. Name, Classification, Containment procedures, description.

Elevator Pitch: This SCP is a beach sixty miles south of Long Beach, California upon which, no matter how long an individual walks across the beach, the water can never be reached. However, the water always appears to be no more than eighty to ninety yards away. The actual anomaly is slightly more interesting than that, as you'll see in the central narrative below.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: Through a series of audio logs between expeditionary personnel and command, as well as autopsy reports, readers will follow teams of research personnel sent to explore SCP-XXXX in hopes to discover more about its anomalous nature. The first expeditionary log reveals that the team suffers a casualty by "dry-drowning" around eight km out, and the others are recovered. Autopsy reveals cause of death to be asphyxia by drowning. The second log reveals that the use of a SCBA allows explorers to venture out substantially farther, reaching close to twenty six kilometers before their oxygen tanks reach half-way empty and they have to turn around. The third log follows a team of researchers more well equipped, with oxygen tanks that should last forty-eight hours. The team reports back around fifty-three km out that there is some form of writing in the sand. Later, they report that they can see what they believe to be a boat in the distance, just off shore, however at the fifty-seven km mark three of the five oxygen tanks simultaneously malfunction. The team turns around, holding their breath unless breathing in through the SCBA, which they take turns using to survive. All team members are recovered, and the writing in the sand is sent to linguists for deciphering. Log four, the final log before SCP-XXXX is deemed unfit for exploration, documents the exploration of four research personnel on board a semi-aquatic vehicle designed to withstand high pressure and impact. They make it twenty-six km before the vehicle begins to flood with water. The team is forced to abandon the vehicle and carry on. At the fifty-seven km mark, the lead researcher calls in that there appears to be a tall, disproportionate figure down near the water, henceforth denoted as SCP-XXXX-1. Before command gets a chance to respond, all personnel experience simultaneous SCBA failures, and the hissing of air and screaming of researchers can be heard just before comm connection is lost. Three of the four corpses are recovered and autopsied, and cause of death is determined to be asphyxia by drowning. The fourth cable comes back severed, and there is blood and a torn shred of clothing on the cable.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A beach that kills people by "dry drowning" them is certainly unique. The test logs will serve as something to actually keep readers interested.

Additional Notes: Researchers in the audio logs are tethered by spools of cable so they can be recovered. All feedback still welcome.
